newsitem.title: UK: BA still negotiating on American deal.
newsitem.headline: BA still negotiating on American deal.

text.p: British Airways Plc confirmed Friday it has not yet settled on terms with Britain's Office of Fair Trading for clearance for its proposed alliance with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines.
"We are still in discussions with the OFT," said a spokeswoman. "There are still a number of issues outstanding," she said.
The OFT said Friday it had not yet reported back to Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang, who would then give the final ruling.

The deal is also being examined by regulators in the United States and the European Commission and requires Britain and the United States to agree on an "open skies" airlines trade pact to open up the transatlantic market.
But everything else in the process hinges on the long awaited British ruling.

Lang announced initial proposals in December for clearing the deal, provided that BA and American could reach agreement with the OFT on satisfactory conditions. In particular Lang had proposed that BA and American should "release" up to 168 weekly runway slots at London Heathrow to make more room for transatlantic competition. and invited other airlines and interested parties to comment to the OFT.
Rival airlines have said more concessions need to be made at Heathrow if BA and American are to be prevented from dominating the British transatlantic market with 62 percent of all current capacity.
Access to Heathrow is also the key issue in the open skies negotiations, which were adjourned last week.
But British Airways Plc declined to comment Friday on a report that its chief executive has asked Britain to break the regulatory logjam.
